title: The best JustCall alternatives in 2026
summary: The best JustCall alternatives for outbound sales in 2026, ranked. Artisan runs calling inside one AI-driven system, plus Nooks, Orum, Salesfinity and more.
body_markdown:
The best JustCall alternative for outbound sales is Artisan, because it consolidates the dialer, the data, and the sequencer into one AI-run system rather than a phone-and-SMS app you wire to other tools. Calls run as steps in an AI-driven sequence, with Ava doing the prospecting around them, on usage-based pricing. For pure parallel-dial floors, Nooks and Orum go wider.

## Why do teams look for a JustCall alternative?


JustCall is a capable SMB phone and SMS platform. It gives smaller sales and support teams voice, texting, a sales dialer, and CRM integrations in one app, priced per seat from Team $29 to Pro Plus $89/user/month annually, with a custom SalesPro tier. The reason outbound teams look elsewhere is what sits outside the phone. JustCall dials and texts, but it does not source leads, enrich them, write the outreach, or handle replies. These jobs live in a data tool, a sequencer, and a rep's inbox, and JustCall is one connector among them. As a team scales outbound, it wants fewer moving parts, faster dial modes, and the calling wired directly into a cadence rather than into a stack it maintains by hand.


## How we chose


Four tests, weighted for outbound sales rather than SMB telephony:


-


How much of the job the tool does. Dialing and texting only, or sourcing, writing, dialing, and reply handling.


-


Where calling lives. Calls as steps inside a sequence beat a standalone phone app.


-


Pricing transparency. Published pricing beats gated quotes.


-


Compliance and scale fit. Number pooling, do-not-call (DNC) checks, calling-hours enforcement, and CRM owner mapping matter across a growing team.


## What is the best overall JustCall alternative?


### 1. Artisan: Calling inside one AI-run outbound system


Artisan is the strongest JustCall alternative for outbound because it collapses the stack. Instead of a phone app plus a data tool plus a sequencer, an AI business development representative (BDR) named Ava sources leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, enriches them with waterfall email and phone data, writes personalized outreach, dials, handles replies from a knowledge base, and books meetings. Calls run as steps in the same multichannel sequence as email and social media outreach.


The dialer is enterprise-grade. It offers power and parallel dialing up to three lines with AI answer detection, live talking points before the call connects, live transcription, auto-classified outcomes, AI-drafted follow-up email, AI voicemail drop, and automatic area-code matching. Numbers are pooled at the org level with personal callback routing so a return call reaches the right rep. Compliance runs per lead: calling-hours enforcement, DNC checks, consent-aware recording, and carrier spam-reputation monitoring. Numbers are available in the US, Canada, the UK, Mexico, and Colombia.


Pricing is the argument. Artisan is usage-based: Ava's work runs on credits, so you pay for what she actually performs, whether that is qualifying, enriching, personalizing, or sending, and you can try her for free. Over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously, which is what turns a phone into an outbound engine.


**Best for:** outbound teams from startup to enterprise that want one AI-run system instead of a stitched stack, with sales ops running Ava centrally for account executives who never log in.


**Who should pick something else:** teams whose entire day is maximum-volume parallel calling may want a dedicated 5-to-10-line floor.


**Pricing:** usage-based, with a free trial. See[Artisan pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Nooks: The parallel-dialing call floor


Nooks is a leading parallel dialer for teams whose motion is volume calling. It dials multiple lines at once with AI answer detection and runs a virtual salesfloor for live coaching. Nooks raised a $43M Series B. Pricing is demo-gated and billed annually, reported by third parties around $4,000 to $5,000/user/year, the tradeoff for a dedicated floor. See[Nooks pricing and reviews](https://www.artisan.co/blog/nooks-pricing-and-reviews) and[Artisan vs. Nooks](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-nooks) .


**Best for:** sales development representative (SDR) teams that do hundreds of dials a day as their core job.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that also need lead sourcing, email, and reply handling in one tool.


**Pricing:** demo-gated, billed annually; reportedly ~$4,000 to $5,000/user/year.


### 3. Orum: Enterprise parallel dialing across regions


Orum is the enterprise parallel dialer, running 5 to 10 simultaneous lines with AI answer detection, with international dialing on its Ascend tier. It acquired Scout AI in July 2026, extending its conversation-intelligence story. Its live page is gated, with Launch reported around $250/user/month and Ascend custom-quoted. For a global, high-volume call floor, it earns its price. See[Artisan vs. Orum](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-orum) for the full comparison.


**Best for:** large international SDR floors that optimize connect rate above all.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want calls as one step in a broader AI-run cadence.


**Pricing:** gated; Launch reported ~$250/user/month, up to 5 lines; Ascend custom, up to 10 lines.


### 4. Salesfinity: Transparent parallel dialing


[Salesfinity](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-salesfinity-alternatives) publishes its price where most parallel dialers hide it. It runs five lines at $149 or $349/user/month per its pricing page. For a team that is upgrading from JustCall's single-line dialing to a parallel floor without a sales cycle to learn the cost, it is a clean shortlist entry.


**Best for:** teams that want a parallel dialer with pricing they can see up front.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need the surrounding outbound motion, not just faster dials.


**Pricing:** $149 or $349/user/month, five lines, per its pricing page.


### 5. Kixie: Power dialing plus SMS for reps


Kixie is a rep-focused power dialer with local presence dialing, voicemail drop, and SMS, wired tightly into CRMs. It is the closest like-for-like to JustCall's voice-plus-text approach, with a stronger power-dialing emphasis. Reps who live in the CRM and want faster single-line dialing tend to prefer it. See[Kixie vs. JustCall](https://www.artisan.co/blog/kixie-vs-justcall-which-should-you-choose-in-2026) for the head-to-head.


**Best for:** individual reps and small teams that want quick CRM-connected dialing and SMS.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need parallel lines or an AI to run the surrounding cadence.


**Pricing:** demo-gated.


### 6. PhoneBurner: Single-line dialing with spam care


PhoneBurner is deliberately single-line, trading parallel volume for call quality and its ARMOR number-reputation remediation, aimed at the category's biggest worry: spam flagging. For a JustCall team that dials heavily and worries about numbers being flagged, it is a focused upgrade on call quality.


**Best for:** teams that prioritize number reputation and call quality over parallel volume.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want parallel lines or a full outbound system.


**Pricing:** Standard $140, Professional $165, Premium $183/user/month annual.


### 7. CloudTalk: Support and inside teams


CloudTalk is a cloud call-center phone with routing, interactive voice response (IVR), and analytics. It overlaps JustCall on the support and inside-team job, with more call-center depth. If you are leaving JustCall for telephony reasons rather than outbound scope, CloudTalk is a close swap for a heavier support operation.


**Best for:** support and inside teams that need call-center routing and analytics.


**Who should pick something else:** outbound teams that want a dialer wired into prospecting.


**Pricing:** Lite €19, Starter €25, Essential €29, Expert €49/user/month annual.


## Stay with JustCall if...


Keep JustCall if a simple voice-plus-SMS phone is what you need. If your team is small, dials at modest volume, and wants texting and a sales dialer in one affordable app connected to your CRM, JustCall does this well. The alternatives above matter when outbound scales and you want the calling wired into a prospecting motion rather than maintained as one piece of a hand-built stack.


SaaStr shows the payoff of consolidation. It sent 6,892 emails through Artisan, 3,574 of them to new leads, and reported a 3.6% positive response rate and 49.4% social media connection acceptance in roughly six weeks, with calls part of the same AI-driven motion rather than a separate tool. Amelia Lerutte, Chief AI Officer at SaaStr, said: "Email has always been our number one driver. Artisan is now neck-and-neck in both output and closed-won revenue."

## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to JustCall for outbound sales?


Artisan, if you want the dialer inside a system that also sources leads, writes outreach, and handles replies. Calls run as steps in an AI-driven sequence, priced by usage rather than by seat. If your team only needs a high-volume call floor, Nooks and Orum are stronger single-purpose picks with 5 to 10 parallel lines.


### Is JustCall good for outbound sales?


JustCall is a solid SMB phone and SMS platform with a sales dialer. It handles voice and text well for smaller teams. For outbound at scale, it does not source leads, enrich them, write outreach, or handle replies, so these jobs live in other tools. Teams that want fewer moving parts prefer a system where calling is one step in a full cadence.


### What is the best enterprise alternative to JustCall?


For enterprise outbound, Artisan pairs a compliant dialer with central-ops deployment: pooled org-level numbers, CRM owner mapping so calls log to the right rep, automatic DNC and calling-hours enforcement, and SOC 2 Type II attestation. Usage-based pricing keeps costs tied to the work performed rather than to headcount. For a global standalone call floor, Orum's 5-to-10-line dialer with international dialing on its Ascend tier is the specialist choice.


### How does Artisan's dialer pricing compare to JustCall?


Artisan is usage-based: you pay for the work Ava performs rather than for a fixed seat bundle, and the dialer runs inside that same system. JustCall prices per seat by tier per its pricing page, with AI features often on higher tiers; confirm current pricing directly, since it changes often.


### Does Artisan do parallel dialing?


Yes, up to 3 lines with AI answer detection, run as steps inside multichannel campaigns. This covers most outbound teams and goes beyond JustCall's single-line dialing. Nooks dials around 5 lines and Orum reaches 5 to 10, so a team whose entire motion is maximum-volume parallel calling may still prefer a dedicated floor.


### Can one tool replace JustCall and my sequencer?


For outbound, Artisan can. It runs email, social media, and dialer call steps in one AI-driven sequence, with lead sourcing, enrichment, reply handling, and meeting booking in the same platform. This consolidates the dialer, the sequencer, and the data tools JustCall users usually connect by hand. It is not a full company-wide phone system for support the way JustCall or CloudTalk are.


## The bottom line


JustCall is a phone-and-SMS app. If outbound sales is the job, the stronger move is a system that dials as one part of running the whole motion.[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) consolidates the dialer, the data, and the sequencer into one AI-driven engine, with Ava handling sourcing, writing, and follow-up around every call. For a pure parallel-dial floor, Nooks and Orum stay the specialists. See how the[AI sales agent](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) fits together.
